newsitem.title: QATAR: First ship for Qatar's LNG arrives in Ras Laffan.
newsitem.headline: First ship for Qatar's LNG arrives in Ras Laffan.

text.p: A ship due to export the first batch of Qatar's vast liquefied natural gas (LNG) supplies arrived in the Gulf island's Ras Laffan Port on Tuesday.
The ship is due to begin loading on December 22 and depart for Japan two days later, official sources said.
Qatar's first LNG project -- The Qatar Liquefied Natural Gas Company, or Qatargas -- is designed to produce six million tonnes a year dedicated to Japanese customers.

"This highly significant first LNG export from Ras Laffan Port represents a re-shaping of the world's energy supply landscape," Qatari Energy and Industry Minister Abdullah bin Hamad al-Attiyah was quoted as saying by OPEC's news agency.
"Today is a very important and highly symbolic day for Qatar, as it begins a new era, both in LNG exporting and in regional shipping trade," OPECNA quoted him as saying.
Qatar's LNG reserves are the third largest in the world after Russia's and Iran's.
